summary: Discovery call to capture Equinox Clinical constraints for a closed-loop, air-gapped/private deployment. Main concerns: offline update signing, hardware BOM limits (1 RU head node, mixed GPU ages), minimal telemetry, and audit log requirements. Redwood AE + SE explained private deployment variants, suggested signed-image rotation and KMS/HSM integration approaches, and outlined a pilot flow.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Samira, AE at Redwood — Jordan and Aisha from the solutions team are with me. Could folks do quick intros?
[00:00:12] Dr. Priya Malhotra: Sure — Priya here, CTO at Equinox Clinical. We run diagnostic imaging and post-processing pipelines, lots of PII and PHI.
[00:00:20] Oliver Chen: Oliver, infra lead. I'm the one who will actually touch the racks.
[00:00:24] Marta Alvarez: Marta — compliance. SOC 2 and some regional privacy reqs are my main things.
[00:00:28] Diego Ramos: Diego, ops — maintenance windows and change control.
[00:00:33] Samira Khan: Great, appreciate it. Goal today: understand your constraints for a private, air-gapped install and what an update/patch lifecycle looks like. We'll be candid about tradeoffs.
[00:00:43] Jordan Lee: Quick note — when we say "private" here we mean Redwood Private: VPC/on-prem package that can be configured for no outbound egress. But we have different update modes — online pull, signed-image import via USB, or couriered media.
[00:00:58] Priya: We need no outbound by default. Any telemetry must be opt-in and filtered. And updates have to be physically reviewed, signed by our key, and pushed during quarterly maintenance windows.
[00:01:09] Marta: Also need full audit logs for every model change and operator action — immutability preferred.
[00:01:16] Jordan Lee: Understood. We support audit logging and can export logs to your SIEM. The Private package can be configured to store logs locally and then ship via offline transfer. We also support signed artifacts — images and model bundles signed with a key you control.
[00:01:29] Oliver: What's "signed" mean in practice? Are you expecting us to run an HSM or will Redwood manage keys?
[00:01:35] Aisha Patel: We generally recommend customer-managed keys for air-gapped installs. You can use an HSM or KMS appliance; Redwood will verify signatures during the import. If you prefer, we can do key wrap with customer keys — important for compliance.
[00:01:48] Priya: Good, we cannot hand over keys. We have an on-prem HSM.
[00:01:52] Jordan: Perfect — that aligns. We'll provide a signing toolchain that integrates with common HSMs and outputs a signed tarball (model+manifest+checksum). On import we validate the manifest signature before installing.
[00:02:05] Diego: How long does a full model rotation take? We have small maintenance windows — 2 hours every Friday night.
[00:02:12] Jordan: It depends on model size and quantization. A 7B model with quantization and streaming warm-up might take 20–30 minutes to deploy on a single node, but cold KV cache and priming could add time. For larger model swaps you may need an extended window or staged rollout.
[00:02:27] Marta: We prefer staged so we always have a rollback path. Can we pin a canary and then roll back automatically on errors?
[00:02:34] Samira: Yes — Redwood Private supports canary deploys and automatic fallback policies. In an air-gapped setup the coordination is manual, but we can provide tooling that marks a node as canary and validates health checks before enabling route.
[00:02:48] Oliver: Let's talk hardware. We don't have space for big racks — the node has 1 RU for head node and a 2RU GPU sled available. GPUs are mixed: a refurbished A5000 and an older V100.
[00:02:59] Jordan: Mixed GPU generations are workable but affect perf predictability. Our runtime can select kernels and quantization paths per card, but throughput SLOs will vary. For strict latency SLAs we recommend uniform GPU generations.
[00:03:14] Oliver: Budget's tight — replacing fleet isn't feasible for phase 1. Can Redwood optimize for that?
[00:03:18] Aisha: We can generate per-GPU profiles and suggest batch sizes/sequence caps. Also suggest tokenization/quantization to reduce memory. We'll send a sizing spreadsheet after this call.
[00:03:29] Priya: For regulatory reasons we cannot allow outbound debug traces. How granular is telemetry control?
[00:03:35] Jordan: Telemetry is configurable to the field level: errors-only, performance-metrics-only (aggregate), or none. For air-gapped customers you can choose none and still get local traces that you export manually. There may be a tradeoff: without telemetry, automated health-based routing is limited.
[00:03:50] Diego: On updates, we want a deterministic chain: human review -> sign -> physical transfer -> install -> verify -> smoke test.
[00:03:58] Samira: That's the pattern we expect. Our signed-image flow supports manifest verification and pre/post install checks. For the smoke test we can produce a small prompt set to validate output distribution (quality gates).
[00:04:10] Marta: Those prompt sets need to be under our control.
[00:04:12] Jordan: Absolutely — you can supply canonical prompts. We run evals locally against the new model bundle during the maintenance window.
[00:04:19] Priya: Any dependencies on specific OS or BMC access? We have strict out-of-band BMC policies.
[00:04:25] Oliver: Right — Dell iDRAC access is with jump-host only; we don't want vendor staff touching BMC.
[00:04:30] Aisha: For install, we only need standard kexec-style access and an operator with sudo to run the import script. If needed, Redwood can provide exact commands for your change control to approve. No ongoing BMC access required.
[00:04:43] Diego: Patch windows — what's the recommended cadence? Our security team wants monthly patches but operations prefer quarterly.
[00:04:50] Marta: From compliance perspective, critical CVEs should be applied within 30 days.
[00:04:54] Samira: We can support flexible cadence. For critical security updates we recommend an expedited signed-image path; for routine model updates we can queue for quarterly windows and provide release notes.
[00:05:05] Priya: How do you handle firmware or driver updates? Those are often the blockers for our change control.
[00:05:10] Jordan: Firmware and low-level driver updates are in your control. Redwood's bundle can include recommended driver versions, checksums, and version gating. We recommend applying firmware first in a maintenance window, then the software/model bundle after successful validation.
[00:05:22] Oliver: Can the runtime run without CUDA kernels pinned? Our older cards have different driver requirements.
[00:05:28] Jordan: The runtime has multiple execution paths. Where possible we use vendor kernels; for mismatched drivers we can fall back to a quantized, CPU-assisted path but expect slower latency. We'll profile your hardware and provide guidance.
[00:05:41] Diego: On backup and disaster recovery — if the node fails, do we have a fast way to bootstrap from our media?
[00:05:46] Aisha: Yes — Redwood will provide an importable, signed bootstrap image and step-by-step restore playbook. For full DR you can maintain a cold spare with the latest signed artifacts; when you bring it online you validate signatures and swap routes.
[00:05:59] Priya: Now on access controls — RBAC and SSO. We use SAML SSO and strict role separation.
[00:06:05] Jordan: Redwood Private supports SAML/SSO integrations; RBAC can be mapped to your identity provider. For air-gapped installs we support a local identity provider or a sync-only model with periodic export of user mappings.
[00:06:17] Marta: Audit logs — we need tamper-evidence and retention for 7 years for certain actions. Can you sign logs?
[00:06:23] Samira: We can produce signed audit bundles and use append-only logs with hash chaining. We'll provide the architecture diagram. Long-term retention will be your responsibility, but Redwood will supply the signed exports.
[00:06:35] Oliver: Is there any hidden telemetry or phone-home if we choose "no telemetry"?
[00:06:39] Jordan: No hidden phone-home. When configured for no egress, the process will not attempt outbound calls. We do have optional diagnostic packages that you upload to us manually if you want debug help.
[00:06:50] Diego: Licensing and pricing — are there seat counts or just node-based?
[00:06:54] Samira: For Private deployments we price per-reserved node and per-model licensing if there are premium variants. We can give an indicative quote after sizing; we also have enterprise support tiers for faster on-call response.
[00:07:05] Priya: For procurement: we need a template SOC 2 attestation, encryption-in-transit docs, and a list of sub-processors.
[00:07:12] Samira: We'll send our compliance pack. Note that for on-prem deployments sub-processors are limited — we can provide a list and options.
[00:07:19] Marta: Will anything in your hosted control plane have access to PHI?
[00:07:23] Jordan: In the Private install, customer data stays local unless you opt-in to export. The control plane can be configured to be local-only. We can run the management plane in a customer VPC or fully on prem with our private bundle.
[00:07:36] Diego: About model provenance — we need to ensure exact weights provenance and a chain of custody.
[00:07:41] Aisha: Our signing manifest includes model hash, builder metadata, and a provenance URI. You can require builds to include CI/CD signatures.
[00:07:49] Priya: One technical ask — can you checksum the KV cache warmup state so we can validate identical performance between nodes?
[00:07:56] Jordan: We don't checksum live KV state commonly, but we can record cache warmup histograms and a hashed seed of key pages. We'll add that to the checklist as a potential approach.
[00:08:10] Samira: Quick commercial note — if you commit to a 12-month reserved private cluster we can provide a discounted install support package that includes one on-site assistance for the initial build.
[00:08:20] Oliver: May be useful.
[00:08:22] Diego: Who will run the initial on-site build? Redwood or our contractors?
[00:08:25] Samira: Either. Our field engineers can assist under enterprise support, or you can have your integrator run it with our remote guidance. For air-gapped installs we typically provide a runbook and test checklist.
[00:08:36] Priya: Can I get a sample runbook before procurement?
[00:08:39] Jordan: Yes — we'll attach a sanitized sample runbook plus the signed-image import steps.
[00:08:45] Marta: A few clarifying questions on legal: we need indemnity for data breaches if there's negligence.
[00:08:52] Samira: Legal can discuss standard enterprise terms; we have SOC 2 and ISO attestations, and we can negotiate data protection clauses in the enterprise contract.
[00:08:59] Diego: Performance benchmarking — we want to run a local perf test. Can Redwood provide a benchmark harness that runs entirely offline?
[00:09:04] Aisha: Yes — we have an offline benchmarking tool that you can run in your environment; it generates a perf report and token-cost estimates. We can provide the harness as a tarball.
[00:09:14] Oliver: For that harness do you require any telemetry to be uploaded?
[00:09:16] Jordan: No, the harness produces a local report that you can share. If you want Redwood to analyze it, you can upload it manually.
[00:09:24] Priya: Any thoughts on mixed GPU scheduling? If one GPU is slower, will requests pile up?
[00:09:29] Jordan: The scheduler is workload-aware and can route by GPU capability. But it won't magically make a slow card faster; you'll see variability. We recommend capacity planning to avoid hot spots and set per-GPU routing policies.
[00:09:43] Marta: For compliance, all operator actions must be auditable and require two-person approvals for critical changes. Could you support a two-person promotion flow?
[00:09:51] Jordan: We support gated rollouts with approver workflows; in an air-gapped setup approvals are manual, but we can provide a signed approval artifact format so you can record approvers in the manifest.
[00:10:05] Diego: Can we integrate your RBAC with our ticketing system for approvals?
[00:10:10] Aisha: We have webhook hooks and an API for approvals, but in strict air-gapped cases we can exchange signed approval files that your ticketing system stores.
[00:10:19] Samira: Let's pivot to concrete deliverables — Jordan, what do we need to profile to produce sizing?
[00:10:24] Jordan: We'll need GPU model and driver versions, node memory, disk IO numbers, expected QPS and tail latency targets, and typical sequence length distributions. Also preferred maintenance windows and a list of critical prompts for QA.
[00:10:37] Oliver: I'll compile the hardware sheet and power diagram.
[00:10:40] Priya: We'll prepare the compliance requirements list.
[00:10:42] Diego: Ops will provide a list of allowed media transfer methods — encrypted USB, dedicated jump host, or courier.
[00:10:48] Samira: Good. We'll follow up with the checklist and a proposed pilot plan: a 2-week local perf run, then a single-model signed-image rotation in your quarter window.
[00:10:58] Marta: Timeline — procurement needs 2 weeks to review security docs. If you send docs tomorrow we can align for a January pilot.
[00:11:06] Samira: We'll aim to get docs this week.
[00:11:09] Jordan: One last technical note — in air-gapped installs we recommend containerizing the runtime and storing images as OCI tarballs with signature verification. It makes rollback easier.
[00:11:20] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:11:23] Samira: Any other open questions?
[00:11:25] Diego: Not from me.
[00:11:26] Oliver: No.
[00:11:27] Marta: Nope.
[00:11:28] Priya: Only that we will need specific language about data residency in the contract.
[00:11:32] Samira: Noted. We'll include residency clauses in the draft.
[00:11:36] Samira: Okay, quick recap — Samira to send compliance pack, signed-image process doc, and sizing spreadsheet by 2026-12-03. Equinox will send hardware BOM, rack diagrams, and maintenance windows by 2026-12-06. Jordan will draft model rotation checklist by 2026-12-07.
[00:11:52] Diego: That works.
[00:11:54] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and schedule the readiness call. Bye.
[00:11:59] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[00:12:01] -- End of recorded segment (call continued with private admin items)

Notes on transcript imperfections: some product names transcribed as "Redwood Privatee" or "Redwood Dedicat" in earlier automated notes; KV cache occasionally transcribed as "K V cache". There were a couple of small crosstalks and overlapping talk during the hardware discussion.
